newsitem.title: USA: PairGain slips, Soundview cites pricing concerns.
newsitem.headline: PairGain slips, Soundview cites pricing concerns.

text.p: Shares of PairGain Technologies Inc dropped nearly 17 percent after a SoundView Financial Group analyst raised concerns about pricing pressure, analysts said.
PairGain, which was the most heavily-traded Nasdaq issue at midday, fell 3-1/2 to 17-5/8.
SoundView analyst Chandan Sarkar said he has become more cautious on PairGain but has not changed the rating or earnings estimates.

Tustin, Calif.-based PairGain produces a line of products which allows telephone companies and owners of private networks to transmit high-speed data over ordinary copper wires with the same quality previously only available over fiber optics.

The company's stock has been battered in recent weeks since the PairGain said in a presentation at a Hambrecht & Quist technology conference that it could see competitive pricing pressure, analysts said.
PairGain's stock has falled sharply from a high of 42-1/2 at the end of January.

"There's been some concern about increasing pricing pressure. I don't think PairGain is in bad shape ... but there are some competitors who are becoming major players in their arena," said Michael Davies, an analyst with Utendahl Capital Partners LP.

PairGain faces growing competition from companies such as U.S. Robotics Corp and Adtran Inc, analysts said. Although these firms pose a competive threat to PairGain, they also may see their gross margins pressured by price cuts in high speed digital service, one analyst said.
U.S. Robotics lost 1-1/4 to 64-7/8. Adtran lost 3-3/8 to 28-5/8.
